summary: The recorded base already filtered completed PendingRequest futures at group dequeue and between per-request encodes, preserving part of the referenced upstream candidate. An executed post-lock race showed that a future completed while waiting for encode_dispatch_lock was still broadcast and included in batch_encode. The dispatch path now re-filters the group under the lock and rebuilds the request list. Deterministic regressions exercise the actual PendingRequest and dispatch paths and verify that timed-out or completed requests reach neither sock_send nor the encoder while live requests complete.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before baseline on the recorded base plus new tests: dequeue and per-request guards passed, while the post-lock test failed because batch_encode received ['completed', 'live'] instead of only ['live']. Raw output: reports/j-472949ac8a49/raw/before-focused-corrected.txt

Passing-after run: all three actual dispatch races passed, recording broadcast and encoder calls and confirming live futures completed. 3 passed. Raw output: reports/j-472949ac8a49/raw/after-focused.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The issue is an asyncio scheduler race reproducible at the CPU dispatch seam. Tests exercised actual PendingRequest, EncoderScheduler worker, encode_dispatch_lock, sock_send call sites, batch_encode, and per-request encode without model weights or GPU kernels.

remaining_limitations: No real tensor-parallel workers, model weights, HTTP transport, or GPU execution were used. Broadcast and encoder exclusion were verified at their production Python call sites with deterministic test doubles; distributed collective behavior and model semantics were not in scope for this scheduler race.
